Terms.metaDescription: Terms of use and disclaimer for the Monitor Tester display testing utility.
Terms.title: Terms of Use
Terms.description: Please review the following terms and guidelines for using the Monitor Tester web utility and its diagnostic tools.
Terms.acceptanceText: By accessing and using Monitor Tester, you acknowledge and agree to these terms. If you do not agree with any part of these terms, please discontinue use of the website.
Terms.natureOfServiceText: Monitor Tester is an open web utility designed to assist users in visually evaluating display panels using browser-renderable test patterns, motion simulations, and client-side calculations. These tests are intended for visual screening and self-diagnosis.
Terms.noCalibrationTitle: Not a Replacement for Hardware Colorimeters
Terms.noCalibrationText: Browser-based software cannot replace physical spectrophotometers, hardware colorimeters (such as Calibrite or Datacolor Spyder), or optical oscilloscopes. Monitor Tester does not generate ICC color profiles, read physical photometric nits, or certify absolute color accuracy (Delta-E).
Terms.disclaimerText: Monitor Tester is provided on an 'AS IS' and 'AS AVAILABLE' basis without warranties of any kind, whether express or implied. While we strive for precision, test results may vary based on operating system display scaling, GPU driver configurations, browser hardware acceleration, and ambient lighting conditions.
Terms.manufacturerText: Display manufacturers enforce their own specific warranty terms regarding pixel defects (such as ISO 9241-307 Class 1 or Class 2 standards, which often define minimum thresholds of stuck or dead subpixels before an RMA is authorized). Identifying a defect on Monitor Tester does not automatically guarantee warranty replacement by your device manufacturer.
Terms.openSourceText: The underlying source code of Monitor Tester is licensed under the open-source MIT License. You are free to inspect, review, and fork the source code in accordance with the license.

Home.howItWorksSubtitle: Follow three practical preparation steps to ensure reliable visual inspection before evaluating your display.
Home.step1Desc: Clean dust and smudges from the screen surface. Set your operating system to native resolution and 100% display scaling.
Home.step2Desc: Toggle fullscreen mode (press F11) so browser toolbars, tabs, and operating-system taskbars do not obstruct edge pixels.
Home.step3Desc: Dim room lighting when checking backlight bleed and contrast. Inspect the panel from both direct and off-axis angles.

Home.aboutTitle: Online Screen Test & Monitor Diagnostic Tool
Home.aboutLead: Screen Tester is a free online tool designed for comprehensive display and monitor testing directly in your web browser, with no software or drivers required.
Home.aboutP1: Screen Tester is a free online tool for checking your screen, monitor, or display directly in your web browser. It provides visual tests for common display issues such as dead pixels, colors, brightness, contrast, refresh rate, and screen ghosting.
Home.aboutP2: The tool is useful for checking new or used monitors, laptop displays, gaming screens, and other displays without installing additional software. The tests provide visual inspection patterns and should be treated as a practical reference rather than laboratory-grade hardware measurements.
Home.aboutLimitationsDesc: All tests provide visual diagnostic patterns for human inspection under controlled viewing conditions. Screen Tester does not replace optical hardware sensors (such as spectrophotometers, colorimeters, or photodiode oscilloscopes) and does not modify operating-system color profiles. For optimal results, clean your screen, inspect in fullscreen mode (F11), and verify display scaling is set to 100%.

dead-pixel-test.metaTitle: Dead Pixel Test – Check Dead & Stuck Pixels Online
dead-pixel-test.metaDescription: Free online dead pixel test for monitors and screens. Inspect full-screen solid RGB, black, and white backgrounds to detect dead pixels and stuck subpixels.
dead-pixel-test.title: Dead Pixel Test
dead-pixel-test.description_p1: A dead pixel test helps you quickly find defective, dark, or stuck subpixels on your monitor or laptop display. This test displays full-screen pure colors to make any defective pixel immediately visible.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Ensure your screen is clean before starting. Dust can look like dead pixels.
HOW TO USE: Click or use Space / → to cycle through the test colors.

WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: Carefully scan the entire screen for tiny dots that don't match the background color. A black dot on a white background is typically a dead pixel. A bright dot on a black background is typically a stuck pixel.

color-test.metaTitle: Monitor Color Test – RGB Primary & Secondary Color Palettes
color-test.metaDescription: Test monitor color purity and saturation balance across primary (Red, Green, Blue) and secondary (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow) hues.
color-test.title: Color Test & Visual Calibration
color-test.description_p1: Run an online color test to evaluate RGB color reproduction and visual calibration balance across your display. Cycle through primary and secondary full-screen color fields to spot tint shifts, color banding, and uniformity variations.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Cycle through the colors using Space or →.
HOW TO USE: Look for uneven saturation across the screen.
WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: Check the grayscale patterns for any unwanted color tints (e.g., the gray looking slightly pink or blue). Ensure that primary colors look vibrant and accurate without bleeding.
ABOUT THIS TEST: Provides reference patterns for visual inspection. It does not measure physical panel color accuracy (Delta E).

brightness-test.metaTitle: Monitor Brightness Test – Black Level Clipping Calibration
brightness-test.metaDescription: Calibrate monitor brightness and black level thresholds (levels 1–5) to prevent shadow crushing and washed-out blacks.
brightness-test.title: Brightness & Black Clipping Test
brightness-test.description_p1: This test calibrates your monitor's brightness (black level offset) and evaluates luminance capability. Setting brightness properly ensures deep, inky blacks without crushing shadow details into pure black or washing out dark scenes.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK (PLUGE BARS): On the default PLUGE pattern, inspect the vertical bars against the black background. Bar 0% is true reference black. Adjust your monitor's physical Brightness setting until Bar +2% (RGB 5) is just barely discernible from black.

BLACK CRUSH WARNING: If you cannot distinguish Bar +1% or Bar +2% from the background, your brightness is set too low (shadow details are crushed into pure black). If the black background looks glowing or gray, your brightness is set too high (washed-out black level).
1% SHADOW RAMP: Switch to the 1% Shadow Ramp mode to check fine near-black steps (0% to 10%) and identify your display's exact black clipping threshold.

PEAK LUMINANCE & ABL: Switch to Peak & ABL Windows to test sustained full-screen white (100%) versus a 10% peak window. Notice whether your OLED, mini-LED, or laptop display dims due to Automatic Brightness Limiting (ABL).
brightness-test.description: Calibrate display brightness floor and prevent dark shadow detail crushing.

contrast-test.metaTitle: Monitor Contrast Test – Contrast Ratio & White Saturation
contrast-test.metaDescription: Calibrate monitor contrast and white level separation. Ensure near-white highlights (250–254) are visible without clipping.
contrast-test.title: Contrast & White Saturation Test
contrast-test.description_p1: This test helps you configure your monitor's contrast ratio and gamma response by displaying a 25-step gradient grid from 0% pure black to 100% pure white.
contrast-test.inst1: Inspect the grid blocks to ensure adjacent contrast steps are visually distinct.
contrast-test.inst2: Adjust your monitor's Contrast setting so that blocks 92% and 96% do not blend into 100% white.
contrast-test.inst3: Toggle numerical percentages or switch between brightness and contrast modes using the controls below.
contrast-test.description: Calibrate dynamic range, peak white clipping, and highlight contrast separation.

ghosting-test.metaTitle: Monitor Ghosting Test – UFO Pixel Response Time & Overdrive
ghosting-test.metaDescription: Free online monitor ghosting test. Benchmark pixel response time, trailing artifacts, and overdrive overshoot with moving UFO patterns.
ghosting-test.title: Monitor Ghosting & Overdrive Test
ghosting-test.description_p1: This monitor ghosting test evaluates pixel response times and motion clarity. By watching moving patterns at different speeds, you can easily identify trailing ghosting artifacts or overshoot (coronas) caused by aggressive monitor overdrive settings.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Focus your eyes on the moving blocks. Do not stare statically at the center of the screen.
HOW TO USE: Look for trailing shadows (ghosting) behind the moving blocks.

WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: If you see a bright/inverted colored trail, this is inverse ghosting (overshoot), usually caused by setting your monitor's overdrive setting too high. Adjust the speed and contrast controls to test different pixel transition scenarios.
ABOUT THIS TEST: This is a visual aid for detecting ghosting. A web browser cannot precisely measure pixel response time (GtG or MPRT) in milliseconds.
ghosting-test.description: Test LCD pixel response time, trailing ghost artifacts, and overdrive overshoot coronas.

refresh-rate-test.metaTitle: Refresh Rate Test – Check Real-Time Monitor Hz (60Hz to 360Hz)
refresh-rate-test.metaDescription: Test your monitor refresh rate online. Measure exact frame rate, browser vsync timing, and hardware refresh rate in Hertz (Hz).
refresh-rate-test.title: Refresh Rate Test
refresh-rate-test.description_p1: This refresh rate test measures your monitor's active refresh rate (Hz) and frame synchronization directly inside your browser. Verify whether your display is properly running at its advertised 60Hz, 144Hz, 240Hz, or higher refresh rate.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Browsers usually cap rendering at your primary monitor's refresh rate (e.g., 60Hz, 120Hz, 144Hz).
HOW TO USE: Make sure you do not have background video playback running, as some browsers down-clock animations to match video framerates.

WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: For multi-monitor setups, drag the browser window to the screen you want to test. If the reading is significantly lower than expected, check your OS display settings or GPU control panel to ensure your refresh rate isn't artificially capped.
ABOUT THIS TEST: This test estimates refresh rate based on browser rendering timing (requestAnimationFrame). It is a software estimate, not a direct hardware measurement.

backlight-bleed-test.metaTitle: Backlight Bleed Test – IPS Glow vs Light Bleed Inspector
backlight-bleed-test.metaDescription: Inspect corner light leakage, bezel pinch backlight bleed, and IPS glow in full-screen pure black in a dark room.
backlight-bleed-test.title: Backlight Bleed Test
backlight-bleed-test.description_p1: This test renders a pure black screen. It is designed to expose backlight bleed, clouding, or IPS glow that typically affects LCD/LED panels.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: This test must be performed in a completely dark room.
HOW TO USE: Set your monitor to its standard or calibrated brightness level (do not force 100% brightness unless that is how you normally use it).

WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: Look at the corners and edges of the screen. Backlight Bleed appears as distinct patches of white/yellow light leaking from the bezel. IPS Glow shifts and changes intensity as you move your viewing angle.

bright-pixel-test.metaTitle: Bright Pixel Test – Find Hot & Lit Pixels on Dark Screens
bright-pixel-test.metaDescription: Detect permanently lit bright subpixels and hot pixels using dark gray and pure black reference screens.
bright-pixel-test.title: Bright Pixel Test
bright-pixel-test.description_p1: A bright pixel (also called a hot pixel) occurs when a liquid crystal subpixel or OLED emitter is permanently stuck in the on state, emitting light against dark and black backgrounds.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Test in a dimly lit room for maximum visual contrast against the dark background.
HOW TO USE: Press Space or → to cycle between pure black, dark gray, and single-channel RGB isolation masks.
WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: An illuminated dot on a black screen is a bright or stuck subpixel. Click 'Mark Defect' in the control bar to record its exact coordinates.

stuck-pixel-test.metaTitle: Stuck Pixel Test – Detect Stuck Subpixels (RGB & Colors)
stuck-pixel-test.metaDescription: Test your monitor for stuck subpixels with pure solid color fields. Identify subpixels permanently locked in red, green, blue, or magenta.
stuck-pixel-test.title: Stuck Pixel Test
stuck-pixel-test.description_p1: A stuck pixel test helps you inspect your screen for individual subpixels that remain continuously illuminated with red, green, or blue light. Inspect dark backgrounds and color channels to distinguish stuck subpixels from dead pixels.
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Ensure your screen is clean before starting. Dust can look like pixel defects.
HOW TO USE: Press Space or → to cycle between dark fields and primary color masks.
WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: An illuminated pinpoint of red, green, or blue on a black background is a stuck subpixel. If detected, you can attempt visual cycling using our Stuck Pixel Fixer tool.

uniformity-test.metaTitle: Screen Uniformity Test – Dirty Screen Effect (DSE) & Grays
uniformity-test.metaDescription: Inspect display brightness uniformity, vignetting, and dirty screen effect (DSE) across 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%, and 100% white reference screens.
uniformity-test.title: Screen Uniformity & DSE Test
uniformity-test.description_p1: This test displays stepped grayscale backgrounds to help identify backlight bleeding, edge darkening (vignetting), and Dirty Screen Effect (DSE).
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Check the corners and edges on the 5% and 10% dark grays for clouding or light bleed.
HOW TO USE: On the 20% and 50% grays, look for splotches, bands, or "dirty" smudges across the center of the screen (DSE).
WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: On the 100% white screen, check if any section of the screen looks warmer (pink/yellow) or cooler (blue) than the rest.
ABOUT THIS TEST: This test provides reference backgrounds for visual inspection. It does not measure physical panel luminance variance.

black-level-test.metaTitle: Black Level Test – 0% to 5% Shadow Detail Thresholds
black-level-test.metaDescription: Calibrate near-black luminance thresholds (RGB levels 1 to 5) to reveal dark video and game shadow details.
black-level-test.title: Black Level Test
black-level-test.description_p1: This test helps you configure your monitor's black level (brightness) setting. It displays extremely dark shades near pure black.
black-level-test.inst1: Turn off room lights or reduce glare on the screen.
black-level-test.inst2: Adjust your monitor's 'Brightness' setting until you can barely distinguish block 1 from the pure black background.
black-level-test.inst3: If blocks 1-5 look identical to the background, your blacks are being crushed.

white-level-test.metaTitle: White Level Test – 95% to 100% Highlight Saturation Check
white-level-test.metaDescription: Inspect near-white luminance steps (levels 250 to 254) to ensure high-brightness details are not blown out or clipped.
white-level-test.title: White Level Test
white-level-test.description_p1: Use this pattern to adjust your monitor's Contrast control and check for near-white clipping. The test displays progressively darker shades near pure white so you can verify that highlight detail remains visible.
white-level-test.inst1: Open your monitor's on-screen display (OSD) and locate the physical Contrast control.
white-level-test.inst2: Adjust Contrast while viewing the near-white squares (252–254) against the pure white (255) background.
white-level-test.inst3: Reduce excessive contrast to prevent highlight clipping, ensuring near-white detail remains distinguishable from pure white where possible.

grayscale-test.metaTitle: Grayscale Test – 256 Gray Level Neutrality & Tint Check
grayscale-test.metaDescription: Test monitor grayscale neutrality from 0 to 255. Detect pink/green color casts and banding in monochrome tones.
grayscale-test.title: Grayscale Test
grayscale-test.description_p1: This test displays neutral grayscale backgrounds. It helps you check if your monitor suffers from unwanted color tints in its gray rendering.
grayscale-test.inst1: Cycle through the gray levels using Space or right arrow.
grayscale-test.inst2: Look for pink, blue, or green tints in what should be neutral gray.
grayscale-test.inst3: Use your monitor's RGB balance controls to correct any color cast.

saturation-test.metaTitle: Color Saturation Test – Chroma Clipping & Vividness Check
saturation-test.metaDescription: Assess color saturation thresholds across RGB and CMY channels to identify clipping in ultra-vivid highlights.
saturation-test.title: Saturation Test
saturation-test.description_p1: This test displays a continuous color spectrum and stepped saturation blocks for primary colors.
saturation-test.inst1: Check the smooth spectrum for obvious banding or harsh transitions.
saturation-test.inst2: Look at the individual saturation steps to ensure distinct differences between blocks.
saturation-test.inst3: Adjust your monitor's saturation/vibrancy settings if colors look washed out or overly neon.

gamma-test.metaTitle: Monitor Gamma Test – Visual Gamma 2.2 Calibration Check
gamma-test.metaDescription: Test display gamma tracking against standard Gamma 1.8, 2.2, and 2.4 reference patterns without hardware colorimeters.
gamma-test.title: Gamma Visual Check
gamma-test.description_p1: This visual test helps you evaluate your monitor's gamma tracking and midtone balance against standard curves. A gamma of 2.2 is the standard for sRGB and Windows PCs; objective calibration requires external hardware.
gamma-test.inst1: Enter fullscreen and move away from the monitor, or squint your eyes until the top lines blur into a solid gray.
gamma-test.inst2: Compare the blurred top half to the three solid blocks below.
gamma-test.inst3: The block that perfectly matches the brightness of the blurred top half indicates your monitor's approximate gamma.
gamma-test.inst4: ABOUT THIS TEST: This tool relies on human visual perception and optical blending. It provides visual evaluation and is not a replacement for a hardware colorimeter or spectrophotometer.

motion-blur-test.metaTitle: Motion Blur Test – MPRT Persistence & Motion Clarity
motion-blur-test.metaDescription: Test monitor motion blur and MPRT persistence with high-speed moving line patterns. Evaluate eye-tracking motion blur.
motion-blur-test.title: MPRT & Motion Blur Persistence Test
motion-blur-test.description_p1: Assess how well your monitor handles fast motion without blurring or smearing details.
motion-blur-test.inst1: Track the moving blocks with your eyes.
motion-blur-test.inst2: Look at the small inner square. If the edges blur completely, your monitor has a slow pixel response time.
motion-blur-test.inst3: Adjust speed and contrast to test under different panel overdrive scenarios.
motion-blur-test.description: Test moving picture response time (MPRT), sample-and-hold blur persistence, and eye-pursuit clarity.

hdr-capability-test.metaTitle: HDR Hardware & Signal Detector – OS & Browser Capabilities
hdr-capability-test.metaDescription: Audit whether your monitor, OS compositor, and browser support HDR, 10-bit color buffers, Wide Gamut (DCI-P3/Rec.2020), Canvas P3, and video codecs.
hdr-capability-test.title: HDR Hardware & Signal Detector
hdr-capability-test.description_p1: Comprehensive hardware, OS compositor, and browser pipeline diagnostic tool. Probes CSS dynamic-range, Wide Color Gamut (Rec.2020 / DCI-P3), buffer bit depth, Canvas P3 support, WebGL float buffers, and HDR video decoding capabilities.
hdr-capability-test.inst1: Review the real-time probed compositor state and buffer metrics.
hdr-capability-test.inst2: If HDR is reported Inactive, press Win + Alt + B on Windows or enable HDR in macOS Display Settings.
hdr-capability-test.inst3: Check the video codec compatibility matrix to verify hardware-accelerated HDR playback.

display-info.metaDescription: View detected screen resolution, device pixel ratio (DPR), color depth, GPU renderer, and browser capabilities.
display-info.title: Display Information
display-info.description_p1: This data is read directly from your browser's Web APIs. It represents what the browser can detect about your display setup. Note that operating system scaling settings (e.g., Windows UI scaling at 125% or macOS Retina scaling) will affect the "Logical Resolution" reported here.

gradient-test.metaDescription: Identify color banding artifacts and verify smooth 8-bit, 10-bit, or FRC color transitions across linear gradients.
gradient-test.title: Gradient Banding Test
gradient-test.description_p1: Displays a perfectly smooth 24-bit (16.7 million colors) gradient. On lower quality panels or with restricted bit-depth settings, you will see banding (distinct vertical or horizontal lines instead of a smooth transition).
instructions: WHAT TO CHECK: Look closely at the transition from black to the target color.
HOW TO USE: A true 10-bit or high-quality 8-bit+FRC panel will display a buttery smooth transition.
WHAT YOU MAY NOTICE: If you see obvious vertical stripes (stair-stepping), your display is struggling with color depth. Use Space or arrow keys to cycle gradients.

vrr-test.metaTitle: VRR & Adaptive Sync Test – G-Sync & FreeSync Visual Check
vrr-test.metaDescription: Inspect Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), Nvidia G-Sync, and AMD FreeSync operation with moving pendulum patterns.
vrr-test.title: VRR / Adaptive Sync Visual Inspection
vrr-test.description_p1: This test helps you visually inspect variable refresh rate behavior and animation frame pacing under changing frame workloads. Browser animation timing can provide evidence about frame pacing consistency, but cannot prove that a specific VRR hardware mode is engaged.
instructions: SETUP GUIDANCE: 1. Enable VRR / FreeSync / G-Sync Compatible in your monitor's OSD menu. 2. Enable Variable Refresh Rate or G-Sync in Windows/GPU control panel. 3. Enter Fullscreen for optimal frame presentation.
MOTION WORKLOADS: Switch between Low (30 FPS), Medium (60 FPS), High (Max rAF), and Dynamic Sweep workloads to observe frame pacing stability across varied refresh rates.
WHAT TO WATCH FOR: Watch the vertical bars and pendulum. Notice whether the motion remains fluid and tear-free, or exhibits tearing, stutter, judder, or uneven pacing.

hdr-test.metaDescription: Inspect display specular highlight roll-off, tone mapping clipping, 10% APL peak luminance burst, and near-black shadow detail.
hdr-test.title: HDR Visual Calibration & Highlight Inspection
hdr-test.description_p1: Controlled optical visual test suite for inspecting the physical display panel's response to HDR signals. Evaluate specular highlight clipping points, 10% APL peak white burst luminance, PQ / EOTF tone curve gradation, and near-black shadow detail.
instructions: VIEWING CONDITIONS: Dim ambient room lighting so your eyes can distinguish subtle specular highlight targets and near-black shadow steps.
SPECULAR HIGHLIGHT CLIPPING: Inspect the 90% through 100% Peak White swatches. Target reticles should remain discernible without blending into solid clipped white.
10% APL PEAK LUMINANCE: Switch to the 10% APL window to evaluate local dimming, peak nit boost headroom, and halo blooming against a pure black background.

near-black-test.metaTitle: Near-Black Shadow Detail Test – Dark Tone Separation Check
near-black-test.metaDescription: Inspect subtle dark-tone separation and shadow details near pitch black to eliminate black crush in games and movies.
near-black-test.title: Near-Black & Shadow Detail Test
near-black-test.description_p1: Inspect subtle dark-tone separation and shadow transition behavior just above reference black. Low-luminance dark steps help identify black crush, elevated black floors, or panel vertical banding without claiming laboratory photometric guarantees.
instructions: VIEWING CONDITIONS: For accurate results, view this test in a dimly lit or dark room to allow your eyes to adapt to subtle dark gradations.
STEP SEPARATION: Inspect steps 0.25%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 3%, 4%, 5%, 6%, 8%, and 10%. Check whether the lowest steps are clearly distinct from true black (0%).
OLED & LCD DETAILS: OLED owners should check for near-black transition smoothness and vertical banding. LCD owners should inspect for elevated black floors or muddy dark detail.

gradient-banding-test.metaTitle: Gradient Banding Test – Smooth Color Ramp Transition Check
gradient-banding-test.metaDescription: Evaluate display bit-depth transitions and color ramp smoothness. Detect harsh contouring and posterization steps.
gradient-banding-test.title: Smooth Gradient & Ramp Transitions Test
gradient-banding-test.description_p1: Evaluate display gradient smoothness and detect unwanted quantization banding, harsh tonal steps, or color shifts. A browser canvas cannot definitively prove panel hardware bit depth, but provides high-fidelity reference ramps for visual inspection.
instructions: GRADIENT MODES: Switch between Horizontal Grayscale, Vertical Grayscale, RGB Primaries, and Dark Shadow (0%–25%) to inspect tonal transitions across ranges.
BANDING VS SMOOTHNESS: Look for distinct vertical or horizontal stripes (stepping) across what should be continuous smooth color ramps.
QUANTIZATION COMPARISON: Toggle the 64-step quantization simulator to contrast intentional digital stepping against your display's native gradient handling.
gradient-banding-test.description: Evaluate multi-stop linear and radial gradient smoothness, tonal continuity, and fine ramp transitions.

text-clarity-test.metaTitle: Text Clarity Test – Subpixel Font Rendering & Fringing Check
text-clarity-test.metaDescription: Inspect font rendering crispness, ClearType subpixel anti-aliasing, and color fringing on standard and unconventional subpixel layouts.
text-clarity-test.title: Text Clarity & Subpixel Rendering Test
text-clarity-test.description_p1: Inspect practical on-screen text rendering clarity, edge sharpness, and subpixel color fringing. Evaluates how your display handles typography across various font sizes and contrast pairings under your current OS scaling settings.
instructions: SETUP & SCALING: Ensure browser zoom is set to 100% (Ctrl+0 / Cmd+0) and your operating system is running at native display resolution.
FONT SIZES & CONTRAST: Inspect paragraph and code samples from 8px to 32px in both positive (dark on light) and negative (light on dark) polarities.
SUBPIXEL FRINGING: Look closely at the vertical edges of black letters on white backgrounds for colored red or blue halos (common on BGR or non-standard subpixel layouts).

tv-overscan-test.metaTitle: TV Overscan & Pixel Mapping Visual Test
tv-overscan-test.metaDescription: Check if your television or external monitor is cropping desktop edges or if scaling is affecting fine-detail rendering.
tv-overscan-test.title: TV Overscan & Pixel Mapping Visual Test
tv-overscan-test.description_p1: Visually inspect whether your television or external display is cropping outer desktop edges (overscan) or applying scaling. Outer borders, corner markers, and high-frequency patches help identify scaling, cropping, or interpolation.
instructions: TV PICTURE SETTINGS: On your television remote, open Picture Settings and set Aspect Ratio to 'Just Scan', 'Screen Fit', 'Dot by Dot', or '1:1' (do NOT use '16:9' or 'Zoom').
BORDER REGISTRATION: Enter Fullscreen. Check if all four outer 1px, 2px, and 5px colored border lines are fully visible around all screen edges.
CHECKERBOARD MOIRÉ: Inspect the 1:1 checkerboard patches in the center and corners. If you see wavy moiré rings or shimmering, the TV is scaling or blurring pixels.

scaling-aspect-test.metaTitle: Scaling & Aspect Ratio Test – Geometric Circle & Grid Check
scaling-aspect-test.metaDescription: Inspect display scaling and aspect ratio integrity (16:9, 16:10, 21:9). Verify perfect circles without egg-shaped distortion.
scaling-aspect-test.title: Scaling & Aspect Ratio Inspection
scaling-aspect-test.description_p1: Inspect display scaling uniformity and geometry to detect non-uniform stretching, squashing, or incorrect aspect ratio modes. Concentric circles and calibrated grid overlays expose anamorphic distortion immediately.
instructions: TRUE GEOMETRY: Inspect the concentric center circles. They must appear perfectly circular. If they look oval or egg-shaped, your display is stretching the image.
ASPECT FRAMES: Switch between 16:9, 16:10, 4:3, and 21:9 reference outlines to verify how your display handles non-native content aspect ratios.

multi-touch-test.metaTitle: Touch Test - Test Your Touchscreen Online
multi-touch-test.metaDescription: Use this free touch test to check touchscreen multi-finger contacts, digitizer tracking, and touch point responsiveness online in your browser.
multi-touch-test.title: Multi-Touch Gestures & Multi-Finger Test
multi-touch-test.description_p1: Use this free touch test to check whether your touchscreen detects multiple fingers and responds correctly to touch input. Inspect active contact points, pointer coordinates, and digitizer tracking in real time.
instructions: FREE TOUCH MODE: Place multiple fingers on the surface simultaneously. Observe the active contact counter, individual pointer IDs, coordinates, and peak simultaneous touch count.
MULTI-TOUCH GRID: Touch different grid cells to verify that simultaneous contacts across separate screen quadrants register accurately without phantom ghost touches.
HOLD & EDGE TARGETS: Test the simultaneous hold challenge (holding 3–5 fingers for 1.5 seconds) and touch the outer perimeter and corners to test digitizer edge rejection.
multi-touch-test.description: Verify simultaneous 10-point multi-touch tracking, pinch, rotate, and gesture responsiveness.

accelerometer-test.metaTitle: Accelerometer Test - Test Your Device Sensor Online
accelerometer-test.metaDescription: Test your phone or device accelerometer online. Inspect real-time 3-axis motion, linear acceleration, and gravity sensor telemetry in your browser.
accelerometer-test.title: Accelerometer Test
accelerometer-test.description_p1: Use this free accelerometer test to check your device motion sensors and acceleration vectors in real time. Inspect 3-axis movement, gravitational pull, and sensor responsiveness directly in your browser.
instructions: START MOTION SENSOR: Click 'Start Sensor' to begin reading motion events. On iOS devices, tap 'Allow' when the browser requests permission to access motion sensors.
2D G-FORCE RETICLE: Tilt your phone or tablet in any direction. The visual reticle puck will displace according to gravitational pull along the X and Y axes.
3-AXIS TELEMETRY: Inspect linear acceleration (excluding gravity) and total acceleration (including gravity) across X, Y, and Z axes to verify sensor responsiveness.

gyroscope-test.metaTitle: Gyroscope Test - Test Your Gyroscope Online
gyroscope-test.metaDescription: Test your device gyroscope online. Check rotation angles, pitch, roll, and yaw orientation telemetry in real time with an interactive horizon gauge.
gyroscope-test.title: Gyroscope Test
gyroscope-test.description_p1: Use this free gyroscope test to check your device rotation and orientation sensors online. Inspect angular movement, tilt angles (pitch, roll, yaw), and rotational tracking in real time.
instructions: ENABLE GYROSCOPE: Click 'Start Sensor' to begin listening to orientation events. Confirm any browser permission prompts on mobile devices.
ATTITUDE INDICATOR: Rotate and pitch your device. The artificial horizon gauge will reflect roll (gamma) and pitch (beta) relative to the horizon plane.
EULER ANGLES: Inspect Alpha (compass yaw 0°–360°), Beta (pitch -180°–180°), and Gamma (roll -90°–90°) to evaluate smooth angular tracking.

vibration-test.metaTitle: Vibration Test - Test Your Phone Vibration Online
vibration-test.metaDescription: Test your mobile phone vibration motor and haptic feedback online. Test short, medium, and long vibration pulses or create custom vibration patterns.
vibration-test.title: Vibration Test
vibration-test.description_p1: Use this free vibration test to check your phone or mobile device vibration motor and haptic feedback online. Test pulse presets and custom vibration patterns to verify tactile response.
instructions: PRESET PULSES: Tap Short (100ms), Medium (300ms), or Long (600ms) to test standard tactile feedback pulses on your mobile device.
CUSTOM SEQUENCE: Enter comma-separated pulse and pause durations in milliseconds (e.g. 200, 100, 200) to test custom rhythmic haptic sequences within safe duration limits.
OBSERVATION CHECK: Because browsers cannot measure physical motor movement, record whether you physically felt the vibration in your hand.

webcam-test.metaTitle: Webcam Test - Test Your Camera Online
webcam-test.metaDescription: Test your webcam and camera online for free. Check live camera video preview, resolution, frame rate, and take private local test snapshots.
webcam-test.title: Webcam Test
webcam-test.description_p1: Use this free webcam test to check your camera stream and video input online. Inspect real-time camera preview, stream resolution, frame rate, and verify camera permissions securely.
instructions: START CAMERA: Click 'Start Camera' to initiate the video stream. Confirm the browser permission dialog to allow video access (microphone access is never requested).
CAMERA SELECTION & MIRRORING: If multiple cameras are attached, select between front and rear cameras. Toggle the mirror button for natural mirror-image viewing.
TELEMETRY & LOCAL SNAPSHOT: Review browser-reported resolution and frame rate. Click 'Snapshot' to capture a private test frame in browser memory for local download.

speaker-test.metaTitle: Speaker Test - Test Your Speakers Online
speaker-test.metaDescription: Test your speakers and headphones online for free. Check left and right stereo sound channels, audio balance, frequency response, and speaker clarity.
speaker-test.title: Speaker Test
speaker-test.description_p1: Use this free speaker test to check your speakers or headphones online. Verify left and right stereo audio channel separation, sound balance, and test tone clarity across frequency ranges.
instructions: SAFE VOLUME WARNING: Start at a low volume level and increase gradually. Avoid sustained high-volume tones through headphones or near-field monitors.
STEREO CHANNEL SEPARATION: Switch between Left Only (pan -1.0), Stereo Center, and Right Only (pan +1.0) to confirm channels are wired correctly and not reversed.
FREQUENCY TEST TONES: Test Low Bass (100 Hz), Mid Range (440 Hz concert A), High Treble (2,500 Hz), and the 4-second frequency sweep to identify speaker buzz or distortion.

microphone-test.metaTitle: Microphone Test - Test Your Mic Online
microphone-test.metaDescription: Test your microphone and audio input online for free. Check live mic volume levels, real-time audio waveform, digital clipping, and record a playback sample.
microphone-test.title: Microphone Test
microphone-test.description_p1: Use this free microphone test to check your mic and audio input online. Verify live microphone volume levels, monitor waveform activity, detect clipping, and test local sound playback securely.
instructions: START MICROPHONE: Click 'Start Microphone' and allow browser audio access when prompted (video is never requested).
INPUT LEVEL & WAVEFORM: Speak or make sound toward the microphone. Verify that the waveform oscillates and the live input meter registers between 30% and 80%.
LOCAL LOOPBACK & OBSERVATION: Record a 5-second sample to listen to your captured audio locally (headphones recommended to avoid acoustic feedback), then record your observation.

reactionTimeTest.metaTitle: Reaction Time Test – Human Reflex & Display Input Benchmark
reactionTimeTest.metaDescription: Benchmark your visual reaction time and input reflex latency in milliseconds across 5 interactive trials.
reactionTimeTest.title: Human Reflex Reaction Time Benchmark
reactionTimeTest.description_p1: Click or tap when the color changes to measure latency.
instructions: Wait for the screen to change from red to green.
Click as fast as you can once it turns green.
Your reaction time will be recorded in milliseconds.
reactionTimeTest.description: Benchmark cognitive visual reaction time in milliseconds with statistical consistency scoring.

reaction-time-test.metaTitle: Reaction Time Test – Human Reflex & Display Input Benchmark
reaction-time-test.metaDescription: Benchmark your visual reaction time and input reflex latency in milliseconds across 5 interactive trials.
reaction-time-test.title: Human Reflex Reaction Time Benchmark
reaction-time-test.description_p1: Click or tap when the color changes to measure latency.
instructions: Wait for the screen to change from red to green.
Click as fast as you can once it turns green.
Your reaction time will be recorded in milliseconds.
reaction-time-test.description: Benchmark cognitive visual reaction time in milliseconds with statistical consistency scoring.

pixel-inversion-test.title: Pixel Inversion & VCOM Flicker Test
pixel-inversion-test.description: Inspect pixel inversion patterns, VCOM voltage calibration, and pixel walk artifacts across LCD and OLED panels.
pixel-inversion-test.metaDescription: Test your monitor for pixel inversion artifacts, VCOM voltage balance, and pixel walk flicker using high-frequency checkerboard patterns.
instructions: Switch through 1x1 dot, 2x2 checkerboard, vertical stripe, and subpixel patterns.
Observe the screen from your normal working distance with the monitor at native resolution.
Notice whether any pattern vibrates, shimmers, or displays faint moving wave bands.
A properly calibrated VCOM voltage will render all gray checkerboards as steady, non-flickering neutral gray.

strobe-crosstalk-test.title: Strobe Crosstalk & BFI Inspection Test
strobe-crosstalk-test.description: Inspect backlight strobing blur reduction, strobe phase alignment, and double-image crosstalk across vertical screen zones.
strobe-crosstalk-test.metaDescription: Test monitor backlight strobing (ULMB, DyAc, ELMB) and Black Frame Insertion for strobe crosstalk and duplicate silhouette ghosting.
instructions: Enable backlight strobing or BFI in your monitor's hardware OSD menu.
Watch the moving target bars across the top, center, and bottom screen tracks.
Check for double-image silhouettes behind the moving bars in each zone.
Inspect which zone has the clearest motion and whether top or bottom shows strobe phase ghosting.

vrr-flicker-test.title: VRR Brightness Flicker & Gamma Shift Test
vrr-flicker-test.description: Diagnose variable refresh rate brightness fluctuations, LFC frame jumps, and OLED gamma shifts.
vrr-flicker-test.metaDescription: Stress test your monitor for VRR brightness flicker and gamma fluctuation during dynamic refresh rate swings.
instructions: Ensure G-Sync, FreeSync, or Adaptive-Sync is enabled in your graphics driver and monitor OSD.
Run the automated framerate sweep between low and high refresh bounds.
Carefully observe the dark gray background and midtone patches for subtle brightness pumping or flicker.
OLED and VA panels are most susceptible to near-black VRR gamma flicker during framerate fluctuations.

pursuit-camera-test.title: Pursuit Camera Sync & MPRT Calibration Track
pursuit-camera-test.description: Calibrate tracking cameras and smartphones to photograph moving objects for scientific MPRT and ghosting measurement.
pursuit-camera-test.metaDescription: Pursuit camera temporal sync track for photographic measurement of monitor motion blur, ghosting, and MPRT.
instructions: Set your camera or smartphone to manual exposure mode with a shutter speed of 1/4 to 1/2 of your panning time.
Track the moving pattern smoothly from left to right as it glides across the display.
Review your captured photo: verify the white vertical graduation ticks form a single crisp vertical line.
When temporal graduation lines are un-smeared, your camera tracking was synchronized, allowing accurate MPRT measurement.

audio-sync-test.title: Audio / Video Lip-Sync Calibration Test
audio-sync-test.description: Calibrate audio-video delay, soundbar latency, and Bluetooth audio lag with millisecond visual and acoustic sweep pulses.
audio-sync-test.metaDescription: Test and calibrate audio-to-video lip-sync delay with visual sweep bars and synchronized 1kHz millisecond beeps.
instructions: Ensure audio output is enabled and unmuted in your browser.
Watch the sweeping radar dial as it crosses the center alignment notch.
Listen for the instantaneous 1 kHz audio beep.
Adjust the millisecond offset slider until the visual alignment and sound occur simultaneously.

gamepad-test.title: Gamepad & Controller Input Test
gamepad-test.description: Test gamepad controllers, analog stick drift, deadzones, trigger axes, and button actuation using the HTML5 Gamepad API.
gamepad-test.metaDescription: Online gamepad and controller tester. Check analog stick drift, deadzone precision, triggers, and buttons in real-time.
instructions: Connect an Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, or generic controller via USB or Bluetooth.
Press any button on the controller to wake the Gamepad API.
Rotate both analog sticks to test circularity error and check resting drift values against the deadzone threshold.
Squeeze analog triggers and press all buttons to verify actuation and responsiveness.

battery-test.title: Battery Health & Power Info
battery-test.description: Check your device's battery level, charging status, estimated time remaining, and power source using the Battery Status API.
battery-test.metaDescription: Online battery health checker. View battery level, charging status, time to full, and power source information in real-time.
instructions: Open the test on a laptop, tablet, or mobile device with a battery.
View the current battery percentage and charging status.
Monitor the estimated time to full charge or time remaining on battery.
Watch the history chart to track battery level changes over time.

network-speed-test.title: Network Speed Test
network-speed-test.description: Test your internet connection speed including download throughput, latency ping, and network type using browser APIs.
network-speed-test.metaDescription: Free online internet speed test. Measure download speed, latency, ping, and connection type directly in your browser.
instructions: Ensure you are connected to the internet via Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Click 'Start Test' to begin measuring latency and download speed.
Results show latency in milliseconds and download speed in Mbps.
Run multiple tests to get consistent averages.

color-blindness-test.title: Color Blindness Simulator
color-blindness-test.description: Simulate 8 types of color vision deficiency including Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, and Achromatopsia using real-time SVG color matrix filters.
color-blindness-test.metaDescription: Free color blindness simulator. Preview how your UI, images, and designs appear to people with different types of color vision deficiency.
instructions: Select a color vision type from the options above.
Observe how colors, gradients, and UI elements change under each simulation.
Use the Compare mode to see normal vision side-by-side with the simulated view.
Check if your designs maintain contrast and readability across all vision types.

screen-recorder.title: Screen Recorder & Screenshot
screen-recorder.description: Record your screen or capture screenshots directly in the browser using the Screen Capture API. Download as WebM video or PNG image.
screen-recorder.metaDescription: Free online screen recorder. Capture your screen as video (WebM) or screenshot (PNG) directly in the browser. No installation required.
instructions: Click 'Start Recording' and select the screen, window, or tab to capture.
Use Pause/Resume to control the recording session.
Click 'Stop' to finish recording and preview the video.
Use 'Screenshot' to capture a single frame as a PNG image.

dark-mode-test.title: Dark Mode / Light Mode Test
dark-mode-test.description: Detect your operating system's dark mode preference, test CSS color-scheme support, and preview UI components in both light and dark themes.
dark-mode-test.metaDescription: Test dark mode detection and theme switching. Check OS preference, CSS color-scheme support, and preview UI in light and dark modes.
instructions: The test automatically detects your OS dark mode preference.
Switch between System, Light, and Dark mode previews.
Inspect sample UI elements—buttons, cards, toggles—in each theme.
Check if your browser supports the CSS color-scheme property.

input-lag-test.title: Display Input Lag & Latency Visualizer
input-lag-test.description: Visualize display pipeline processing delay and click-to-photon screen latency.
input-lag-test.metaDescription: Measure input lag and click-to-photon latency. 10-trial visual reaction test with histogram, average, and statistical analysis.
instructions: Click the gray box to begin the test.
Wait for the box to turn green — do NOT click during the red phase.
Click as fast as possible when you see green.
Complete all 10 trials to see your full statistical results.

ambient-light-test.title: Ambient Light Sensor Test
ambient-light-test.description: Read real-time ambient light levels in lux using the AmbientLightSensor API. Includes a brightness gauge, historical chart, and display brightness recommendations.
ambient-light-test.metaDescription: Online ambient light sensor test. Measure room brightness in lux, get display brightness recommendations, and track light level history.
instructions: Allow sensor permission when prompted by the browser.
The lux reading updates in real-time as ambient light changes.
Move your device closer to or away from light sources to see changes.
Check the recommendation for optimal display brightness based on ambient light.

dpi-calculator.title: DPI / PPI Calculator
dpi-calculator.description: Calculate your monitor's DPI, PPI, dot pitch, and check if it meets the retina threshold for your viewing distance. Includes presets for common displays.
dpi-calculator.metaDescription: Free DPI PPI calculator. Enter screen size and resolution to get pixel density, dot pitch, retina threshold, and angular resolution.
instructions: Select a preset or enter your screen's diagonal size and resolution manually.
Enter your typical viewing distance for retina threshold calculation.
View the calculated PPI, dot pitch, aspect ratio, and subpixel count.
Check whether your display meets the retina threshold at your viewing distance.

subpixel-layout-test.title: Subpixel Layout & Text Fringing Test
subpixel-layout-test.description: Inspect RGB, BGR, QD-OLED, WOLED, and PenTile subpixel structures and diagnose text color halos.
subpixel-layout-test.metaTitle: Subpixel Layout & Text Fringing Test - ClearType & OLED Geometry
subpixel-layout-test.metaDescription: Test display subpixel layout (RGB vs BGR vs QD-OLED vs WOLED) and diagnose text fringing and ClearType antialiasing.
instructions: Select your display panel architecture or use the 1px line gratings to determine subpixel orientation.
Inspect high-contrast text samples across light and dark backgrounds for colored edge fringing.
Follow the ClearType tuning guide to adjust font smoothing for non-standard subpixel layouts.

pwm-flicker-test.title: PWM Backlight Flicker & Eye Strain Test
pwm-flicker-test.description: Detect stroboscopic LED pulse-width modulation flicker and evaluate visual fatigue thresholds.
pwm-flicker-test.metaTitle: PWM Backlight Flicker Test - Stroboscopic Eye Comfort & Shutter Check
pwm-flicker-test.metaDescription: Test for invisible PWM backlight flicker and stroboscopic trails across different brightness levels.
instructions: Observe high-speed moving bars while tracking with your eyes or moving a pen across the screen.
Check for discrete stroboscopic phantom beads indicating PWM backlight modulation.
Use your smartphone camera in Pro mode (shutter 1/1000s+) to expose hidden PWM scanlines.

dead-pixel-mapper.title: Dead Pixel RMA Coordinate & Warranty Mapper
dead-pixel-mapper.description: Interactive full-screen canvas to pinpoint defective pixel coordinates and evaluate ISO 9241-307 warranty eligibility.
dead-pixel-mapper.metaTitle: Dead Pixel RMA Coordinate Mapper - ISO 9241-307 Warranty Checker
dead-pixel-mapper.metaDescription: Pinpoint dead and stuck pixel coordinates, evaluate manufacturer warranty thresholds, and export inspection logs.
instructions: Cycle through solid background colors and click directly on defective pixels to mark their coordinates.
Classify each defect as dead dark, stuck subpixel, or surface dust.
Review ISO 9241-307 warranty compliance and export your defect log for manufacturer RMA claims.

gtg-response-time-test.title: Grey-to-Grey (GtG) Response Time Visualizer
gtg-response-time-test.description: Benchmark pixel transition response times across grey levels and identify overdrive overshoot.
gtg-response-time-test.metaTitle: Grey-to-Grey (GtG) Response Time Test - Overdrive & Ghosting Visualizer
gtg-response-time-test.metaDescription: Benchmark panel pixel response times across dark and light grey transitions to tune monitor overdrive.
instructions: Select standard transition presets (e.g. 0% to 20% VA smear test, or 25% to 75% midtones).
Track the moving block with your eyes to inspect leading and trailing edge clarity.
Adjust monitor OSD Overdrive to eliminate ghost trails without causing bright inverted coronas.

oled-burn-in-calculator.title: OLED Burn-in Risk & Longevity Calculator
oled-burn-in-calculator.description: Calculate OLED and QD-OLED panel degradation probability, lifespan in years, and static HUD hazard hotspots.
oled-burn-in-calculator.metaTitle: OLED & QD-OLED Burn-in Risk Calculator - Panel Longevity Estimator
oled-burn-in-calculator.metaDescription: Estimate OLED and QD-OLED panel lifespan, burn-in risk percentage, and static UI degradation hotspots.
instructions: Select your OLED panel generation (WOLED MLA, QD-OLED Gen 3, AMOLED).
Input your daily usage hours, static UI percentage, and average SDR/HDR brightness.
Review your projected burn-in risk timeline, expected lifespan, and mitigation recommendations.

mouse-polling-test.title: Mouse Polling Rate & Cursor Precision Test
mouse-polling-test.description: Measure real-time mouse USB polling frequency in Hz, tracking jitter, button actuation, and sensor DPI.
mouse-polling-test.metaTitle: Mouse Polling Rate (Hz) & Precision Test - Sensor Jitter & Click Checker
mouse-polling-test.metaDescription: Test mouse polling rate up to 8000Hz, check interval jitter, diagnose double-click chatter, and measure DPI.
instructions: Move your mouse rapidly in continuous circles inside the test pad to measure peak and average Hz.
Inspect interval timing consistency and jitter graphs to ensure smooth frame pacing.
Test mouse buttons for actuation latency and mechanical switch double-click bouncing.

gpu-benchmark-test.title: GPU WebGL 3D Stress & Performance Benchmark
gpu-benchmark-test.description: Real-time 3D particle canvas evaluating sustained frame rate, 1% low FPS, and GPU thermal throttling.
gpu-benchmark-test.metaTitle: GPU WebGL 3D Benchmark & Stress Test - FPS, 1% Lows & Hardware Telemetry
gpu-benchmark-test.metaDescription: Benchmark GPU WebGL performance with 10K–200K rotating 3D particles, 1% low FPS telemetry, and 30s stress test.
instructions: Select a particle stress preset ranging from Light (10K) to Extreme Stress (200K particles).
Observe real-time frame rate, 1% low FPS stability, and frame time variance.
Run the 30-second benchmark to calculate your sustained GPU stability score.

display-certificate.title: Display Inspection Certificate & RMA Report
display-certificate.description: Generate a formal, print-ready display health and inspection certificate for resale verification or warranty claims.
display-certificate.metaTitle: Display Inspection Certificate & RMA Report Generator - Print-Ready PDF
display-certificate.metaDescription: Generate a certified display inspection report with hardware specs, pixel defect counts, and grading.
instructions: Verify auto-detected display specifications including native resolution, color depth, and gamut.
Fill in monitor model, serial number, and manual inspection grading results.
Click 'Print / Save as PDF' to generate an official verification certificate.

osd-calibration-guide.title: Interactive OSD Monitor Calibration Assistant
osd-calibration-guide.description: Step-by-step visual calibration wizard for tuning physical monitor hardware buttons (OSD Menu).
osd-calibration-guide.metaTitle: OSD Monitor Calibration Guide - Step-by-Step Hardware Tuning Assistant
osd-calibration-guide.metaDescription: Calibrate your monitor physical OSD buttons for Brightness, Contrast, Gamma 2.2, 6500K Color, and Overdrive.
instructions: Follow the 6 visual steps using your physical monitor buttons (OSD Menu).
Tune Brightness and Contrast to avoid shadow crushing and highlight clipping.
Calibrate Gamma to 2.2, Color Temperature to 6500K neutral white, and optimize Overdrive.

oled-abl-test.title: OLED ABL & Window Size Benchmark
oled-abl-test.description: Measure OLED and Mini-LED Auto-Brightness Limiter (ABL) throttling across window sizes from 1% to 100% full screen.
oled-abl-test.metaTitle: OLED ABL Benchmark - Auto-Brightness Limiter & Window Size Test
oled-abl-test.metaDescription: Test display Auto-Brightness Limiter (ABL) behavior on OLED, QD-OLED, and Mini-LED screens across standard 1%, 10%, 25%, and 100% window sizes.
instructions: Select a window size preset (1%, 10%, 25%, 100%) or use the fine slider to adjust Average Picture Level (APL).
Observe whether the screen dims or throttles as the white surface area increases.
Enable the Sustained Timer to measure thermal brightness step-downs over 10s to 60s.

new-monitor-wizard.title: 5-Minute New Monitor Inspection Wizard
new-monitor-wizard.description: Step-by-step unboxing acceptance inspection covering Dead Pixels, Backlight Bleed, Uniformity, Text Clarity, and Frame Pacing.
new-monitor-wizard.metaTitle: 5-Minute New Monitor Inspection Wizard - Unboxing Acceptance Test
new-monitor-wizard.metaDescription: Run a complete 5-stage inspection on your new or used monitor to verify dead pixels, IPS glow, 50% gray uniformity, text fringing, and refresh rate.
instructions: Advance through each inspection stage using the Next button or Arrow keys.
Mark 'Pass' or 'Issue Found' at each checkpoint to record your observations.
Review your final Panel Health Grade and generate an official inspection certificate.

color-temperature-test.title: Color Temperature & White Point Comparator
color-temperature-test.description: Compare your monitor's white point against CIE standard illuminants (D50, D55, D65, D75, 9300K) to diagnose color cast.
color-temperature-test.metaTitle: Color Temperature Test - D65 White Point & Kelvin Comparator
color-temperature-test.metaDescription: Visual white point and color temperature tester. Compare 5000K, 6500K D65, and 9300K presets to detect warm, cool, or green/magenta tint.
instructions: Select a target illuminant (D50 Warm, D65 Standard, or 9300K Cool) or use Split View.
Inspect the split-screen comparison against D65 daylight to check if your display has an unwanted warm or cool tint.
Use the Grayscale Steps and Tint slider to evaluate neutrality across the entire luminance range.

temporal-dithering-test.title: Temporal Dithering & FRC Micro-Flicker Test
temporal-dithering-test.description: Expose 6-bit+FRC and 8-bit+FRC temporal pixel pulsing and subpixel shimmer using high-frequency pattern grids.
temporal-dithering-test.metaTitle: Temporal Dithering Test - FRC Micro-Flicker & Eye Strain Checker
temporal-dithering-test.metaDescription: Detect temporal dithering and Frame Rate Control (FRC) on monitors. High-frequency checkerboard patterns reveal pixel shimmer and eye-strain triggers.
instructions: Select the 1x1 Checkerboard, 2x2 Grid, or 8-Bit Micro-Step pattern.
Ensure your browser scaling is set to 100% (1:1 pixel mapping).
Inspect the pattern up close or record with a smartphone camera at 120fps/240fps slow motion to spot active pixel dancing.

hdr-peak-brightness-test.title: HDR Peak Luminance & Highlight Clipping Test
hdr-peak-brightness-test.description: Calibrated ST.2084 PQ highlight step pattern (100 to 4,000 nits) to test HDR tone mapping and highlight clipping.
hdr-peak-brightness-test.metaTitle: HDR Peak Luminance & Clipping Test - 100 to 4000 Nits
hdr-peak-brightness-test.metaDescription: Test HDR highlight clipping and tone mapping across 100, 400, 600, 1000, and 4000 nits. Calibrate your Windows HDR and game brightness sliders.
instructions: Ensure Windows HDR or macOS High Dynamic Range is enabled in your system settings.
Cycle through the luminance tiers from 100 nits up to 4,000 nits.
Verify whether the inner step square remains distinct from the outer target box or blends into a clipped white block.

audio-latency-test.title: Audio Hardware Pipeline & Buffer Latency Inspector
audio-latency-test.description: Inspect Web Audio API hardware driver latency, kernel buffer delay, sample rate (44.1k to 192k Hz), and click-to-sound sync.
audio-latency-test.metaTitle: Audio Latency Test - Web Audio Buffer & Hardware Output Pipeline
audio-latency-test.metaDescription: Measure hardware audio output latency, base kernel latency, sample rate, and audio buffer delay with an interactive sound-pulse test.
instructions: Click 'Initialize Audio Engine' to allow the browser to query your sound card driver.
Review your Hardware Sample Rate, Kernel Base Latency, and Driver Output Latency.
Click the central sound orb to test instantaneous auditory feedback and verify audio-visual synchronization.

eink-refresh-tool.title: E-Ink Screen Refresh & Anti-Ghosting Tool
eink-refresh-tool.description: High-contrast inversion waveform generator designed to purge ghosted pigment microcapsules on E-Ink monitors.
eink-refresh-tool.metaTitle: E-Ink Screen Refresh Tool - Electronic Paper Ghosting Purger
eink-refresh-tool.metaDescription: Clear ghosting on E-Ink and electronic paper displays (Dasung, Boox, Bigme). Run Deep Purge, Regal, or A2 inversion flash cycles.
instructions: Select a waveform mode: Deep Purge (8-phase thorough clean), Regal (quick 4-phase), or A2 (fast inversion).
Click the purge button to execute the full-field contrast cycle.
Photosensitive warning: Look away from the screen while high-contrast flashing is active.

multiTouchTest.title: Multi-Touch Gestures & Multi-Finger Test
multiTouchTest.description: Verify simultaneous 10-point multi-touch tracking, pinch, rotate, and gesture responsiveness.

accelerometerTest.title: Accelerometer Test
accelerometerTest.description: Inspect live 3-axis linear acceleration and gravity vectors reported by device motion sensors.

gyroscopeTest.title: Gyroscope Test
gyroscopeTest.description: Inspect device angular rotation, roll, pitch, and yaw angles via browser orientation APIs.

vibrationTest.title: Vibration Test
vibrationTest.description: Test tactile vibration motor feedback and custom vibration patterns with safe duration limits.

explain.title: WHAT DOES THIS MEAN?
explain.logicalResDesc: Also called CSS resolution, this is the grid your browser uses to render content. OS scaling and browser zoom can make this lower than your physical panel resolution.
explain.physicalResDesc: The physical pixel grid built into your display panel. Running at non-native resolutions involves scaling and can make text appear softer.
explain.dprDesc: DPR is how many physical device pixels are used to draw a single CSS pixel. A DPR of 2 means a 10x10 CSS box uses 20x20 physical pixels.
explain.ppiDesc: Pixel density (PPI) describes how many pixels are packed into each inch of the display. Higher PPI means sharper text and images, assuming the viewing distance is the same.
explain.refreshDesc: Higher resolution increases rendering workload. Higher refresh rate increases frame delivery requirements. The available combination depends on your GPU, connection bandwidth, and display.

troubleshoot.title: TROUBLESHOOTING
troubleshoot.q1: My resolution is lower than expected.
troubleshoot.a1: Check OS display scaling (e.g., 150%). This reduces the logical resolution reported to the browser. Also check browser zoom settings.
troubleshoot.a2: Check that the OS output is set to 4K. If you are mirroring a lower-resolution laptop screen, the external monitor will look blurry.
troubleshoot.a3: Check your cable. Some high resolution + high refresh combinations require DisplayPort 1.4 or HDMI 2.1. Older cables may limit you to 60Hz.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Can a browser detect my monitor's true physical resolution?
faq.a1: Not reliably. Browsers see the logical resolution and scaling factor provided by the OS. If scaling is applied, the physical resolution cannot be guaranteed.
faq.a2: This is common on Windows laptops (e.g., 125% or 150% scaling) to make text readable on high-DPI screens without making everything tiny.
faq.q3: Why is my observed frame timing different from my monitor's refresh rate?
faq.a3: Browser frame timing is affected by system load, power saving, background tabs, and browser behavior. It is an approximation, not a direct hardware query.

BurnInPattern.almostAllLargeOled: Almost all large OLED panels exhibit faint vertical streaks on very dark 5% gray slides due to manufacturing tolerances in the thin-film transistor backplane. This is typical for OLED technology and is virtually invisible in real content.

HdrVisualPattern.displaysSupportingDciP3: Displays supporting DCI-P3 and Rec.2020 render deeper crimson reds, richer emerald greens, and vibrant royal blues.

HdrVisualPattern.inYourMonitorOsd: In your monitor OSD, select an accurate HDR preset (e.g. HDR Cinema, Filmmaker, or HDR Standard) rather than dynamic/vivid modes.
HdrVisualPattern.inTheHighlightClipping: In the Highlight Clipping pattern, reticles in the 94% and 97% swatches should remain visible without blown-out white blooming.

HdrVisualPattern.toneCurveGradationSubtitle: Inspect for harsh quantization stepping, color banding, and tone-curve compression across luminance ranges.
HdrVisualPattern.toneCurveInspectionTip: On high-fidelity 10-bit panels, the continuous ramp should appear completely seamless without vertical quantization bars.
HdrVisualPattern.shadowInspectionTip: If steps 0.5% through 2% appear completely black, your display is crushing shadow details (black crush).

MotionPattern.aDarkOrSmeared: A dark or smeared trail behind moving objects indicates slower liquid crystal transitions (common on VA and older IPS panels).
MotionPattern.aBrightWhiteOr: A bright white or glowing outline ahead or behind the moving block. This means your monitor's physical
MotionPattern.settingIsPushedToo: setting is pushed too high. Lower overdrive one notch (e.g. from "Fastest" to "Fast").
MotionPattern.onVaPanelsAnd: On VA panels and some OLEDs, transitioning from pure 0% black to 5% dark gray takes several times longer than light-to-light transitions, producing purple or pitch-black smears in dark scenes.
MotionPattern.thisIsAVisual: This is a visual diagnostic aid. Web browsers cannot provide laboratory-grade millisecond response time (GtG / MPRT) measurements, which require a high-speed photodiode oscilloscope and a pursuit camera rig.

NearBlackPattern.darkenRoomLightingObserve: Darken room lighting. Observe where subtle dark patches separate from the pitch-black surrounding field.
NearBlackPattern.webBrowsersCanOutput: Web browsers can output mathematically accurate sRGB dark code values (such as RGB 1, 2, 3), but
NearBlackPattern.cannotMeasureThePhysical: cannot measure the physical luminance (nits) or black level output by your display panel
NearBlackPattern.inabilityToDiscernSteps: . Inability to discern steps below 1% or 2% is normal in ambient room light or on displays without professional gamma calibration. Do not assume your panel is defective based on visual inspection alone.
NearBlackPattern.turnOffRoomLights: Turn off room lights and close blinds. In bright rooms, ambient reflections overpower near-black steps.
NearBlackPattern.ifStepsBelow3: If steps below 3% are invisible, check your monitor OSD Gamma preset (standard 2.2 vs sRGB curve) or HDMI Black Level (Full vs Limited).
NearBlackPattern.selfEmissiveOledSubpixels: Self-emissive OLED subpixels turn off completely at 0%. Click the 1% to 5% tiles to inspect for subtle vertical banding.
NearBlackPattern.onVaAndTn: On VA and TN panels, near-black detail may shift or wash out off-axis. Keep your gaze perpendicular to the center.

SaturationPattern.clickAnywhereToCycleTitle: Click anywhere to cycle mode: Combined → Rainbow (Hue) → RGB Steps

ScalingAspectPattern.theBrowserViewportRenders: The browser viewport renders CSS geometric primitives with mathematically equal horizontal and vertical pixel units. However,
ScalingAspectPattern.ifThePhysicalPanel: if the physical panel has an unusual non-square pixel aspect ratio, or if GPU scaling is set to 'Stretch' instead of 'Maintain Aspect Ratio', circles will appear distorted into ovals
ScalingAspectPattern.inspectTheCirclesPhysically: . Inspect the circles physically or with an external ruler to confirm true geometry.
ScalingAspectPattern.ifTheCentralCircles: If the central circles look elongated into horizontal or vertical ellipses, your graphics driver or display OSD is stretching a mismatched resolution.
ScalingAspectPattern.whenRunning169: When running 16:9 content on an ultrawide monitor, ensure your monitor OSD is set to 'Aspect' or '1:1' so pillarbox black bars appear on the sides rather than stretching.
ScalingAspectPattern.inNvidiaControlPanel: In NVIDIA Control Panel or AMD Software, set 'Perform scaling on' to GPU or Display with
ScalingAspectPattern.holdAPhysicalRuler: Hold a physical ruler up to the screen. The width of the 320px outer circle should match its height within 1mm.

SharpnessPattern.theQuickBrownFox: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs. 0123456789
SharpnessPattern.theQuickBrownFox_1: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Clean text should have no color halos along vertical stems.
SharpnessPattern.standardUiTextLook: Standard UI Text: Look for fringing (red/blue edges) caused by non-standard BGR or WRGB subpixel layouts.
SharpnessPattern.bodyCopy14pxText: Body Copy: 14px text rendered cleanly on a calibrated 4K or 1440p monitor should appear sharp as print.
SharpnessPattern.headingTextBoldAnd: Heading Text: Bold and Semibold letterforms should maintain crisp inner negative space without bleeding.
SharpnessPattern.at100NativeScaling: At 100% native scaling, 1px alternating lines should show razor-sharp black and white pixels without soft gray interpolation. If lines look blurry or smeared, verify that your display resolution matches your monitor's native hardware resolution.
SharpnessPattern.standardWindowsMacosSubpixel: Standard Windows/macOS subpixel rendering assumes an
SharpnessPattern.layoutsOrWoledQd: layouts (or WOLED/QD-OLED triangular layouts) can exhibit pink or cyan color halos along vertical text edges.
SharpnessPattern.concentricCircularInterferenceBands: Concentric circular interference bands occur when high spatial frequency patterns beat against display pixel apertures or non-integer OS scaling (e.g. 125% or 150%). At 100% or 200% integer scaling, moiré rings are minimized.

TextClarityPattern.subpixelFontRenderingText: Subpixel Font Rendering & Text Edge Clarity
TextClarityPattern.inspectTextStrokesAt: Inspect text strokes at varying point sizes for color fringing, haloing, or blur.
TextClarityPattern.theQuickBrownFox: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. 0123456789 (ABCDEF)
TextClarityPattern.cleanModernUiTypography: Clean modern UI typography uses subtle anti-aliasing. Look closely at vertical stems (l, t, k) and curves (e, o, s) for color fringing.
TextClarityPattern.thinSerifsAndHigh: Thin serifs and high-contrast stroke transitions test fine pixel resolution. Fine horizontal hair-strokes should remain crisp without breaks.
TextClarityPattern.constDeltaMathSqrt: const delta = Math.sqrt(x * x + y * y);
TextClarityPattern.nonStandardSubpixelLayouts: Non-standard subpixel layouts (e.g. BGR, WOLED, QD-OLED triangular subpixels) often exhibit color fringing (red/green or magenta/cyan shadows) on high-contrast text edges.
TextClarityPattern.pureWhiteTextCrisp: Pure White Text: Crisp edge check
TextClarityPattern.pureRedTextPrimary: Pure Red Text: Primary channel check
TextClarityPattern.pureGreenTextLuminance: Pure Green Text: Luminance channel check
TextClarityPattern.pureYellowTextRed: Pure Yellow Text: Red + Green blend
TextClarityPattern.pureBlackTextHigh: Pure Black Text: High contrast check
TextClarityPattern.deepRedTextNegative: Deep Red Text: Negative contrast check
TextClarityPattern.deepGreenTextNegative: Deep Green Text: Negative contrast check
TextClarityPattern.deepBlueTextHigh: Deep Blue Text: High frequency check
TextClarityPattern.operatingSystemFontAnti: operating system font anti-aliasing engines (such as Microsoft ClearType or macOS Core Graphics)
TextClarityPattern.andDisplayScalingFactors: and display scaling factors. Subtle color fringing on non-standard subpixel layouts (like BGR or OLED pentile/triangular arrangements) is an inherent optical characteristic of font subpixel rendering algorithms, not a defective display panel.
TextClarityPattern.ensureYourDisplayIs: Ensure your display is operating at its physical panel native resolution. Non-native resolutions cause soft, blurry text.
TextClarityPattern.nonIntegerScalingSuch: Non-integer scaling (such as 125% or 175%) can produce subtle shimmering on fine lines. Test at 100% or 200% for integer scaling.
TextClarityPattern.toConfirmYourBrowser: to confirm your browser is set to exactly 100% zoom.
TextClarityPattern.checkYourMonitorOsd: Check your monitor OSD settings. Artificial sharpness filters above 50% often introduce white halo outlines around letters.

UniformityPattern.checkTheFullWhite: Check the full white field for color temperature consistency (e.g., pink or greenish tint variations across left vs right sides).
UniformityPattern.observeThePerimeterAnd: Observe the perimeter and corners for bezel pinch marks, backlight diffusion drop-off, and edge shadows.

ViewingAnglePattern.inspectWhitePointUniformity: Inspect white point uniformity across wide angles. Look for pinkish, yellowish, or bluish tint shifts toward the edges.

PixelInversionPattern.title: Pixel Inversion Patterns
PixelInversionPattern.description: LCD panels rapidly invert subpixel electrical polarities each frame to prevent liquid crystal polarization degradation. Imperfect VCOM balance creates subtle flicker or crawling patterns on these test grids.
PixelInversionPattern.vstripesDesc: Tests source driver column polarity transitions.
PixelInversionPattern.hstripesDesc: Tests gate line row inversion transitions.
PixelInversionPattern.textPhaseDesc: Reveals pixel walk jitter when reading fine text.
PixelInversionPattern.flickerWarning: If the pattern flickers, shimmers, or displays a crawling grid, your display's VCOM calibration voltage is slightly unbalanced.
PixelInversionPattern.notice: Observe from your normal viewing distance. The gray background should appear calm and non-vibrating.

AudioSyncPattern.title: A/V Lip-Sync Calibration
AudioSyncPattern.description: Synchronize display output and audio hardware. When the visual sweep bar crosses the center alignment notch, an instantaneous 1 kHz audio pulse is emitted.
AudioSyncPattern.calibrationTip: Adjust the offset slider until the audible beep and the visual flashing notch occur at the exact same perceptual instant. Positive values delay audio; negative values advance audio.

PursuitCameraPattern.title: Pursuit Camera Synchronization Track
PursuitCameraPattern.description: Pursuit camera tracking simulates the smooth-pursuit motion of human eyes tracking on-screen objects. Capture the moving UFO with a tracking camera to photograph MPRT and ghosting.
PursuitCameraPattern.trackingInstructions: Align your tracking camera so the white temporal tick marks in the upper track stay vertically stationary during your pan. When the ticks form a vertical line in your exposure, tracking sync is achieved.
PursuitCameraPattern.mprtFormula: Motion Picture Response Time (MPRT) is directly proportional to visual smear width divided by panning velocity.
PursuitCameraPattern.cameraInstructions: Pan your camera across the screen at matched speed. When vertical graduation lines align crisply, tracking is synchronized.

StrobeCrosstalkPattern.title: Strobe Crosstalk & BFI Inspection
StrobeCrosstalkPattern.description: Backlight strobing (ULMB, DyAc, ELMB) turns off the backlight during liquid crystal transitions. Strobe crosstalk causes double images when the flash phase does not align with the panel refresh scan.
StrobeCrosstalkPattern.crosstalkDesc: Compare ghost trails in the top, center, and bottom tracks. Fast monitors optimize strobe phase for the center zone, but top and bottom zones often show faint twin silhouettes.

VrrFlickerPattern.title: VRR Gamma Flicker Stress Test
VrrFlickerPattern.description: Adaptive sync alters panel refresh rate in real-time. Because LCD and OLED voltage response varies with refresh cycle duration, rapid framerate swings can induce noticeable luminance flicker.
VrrFlickerPattern.gammaFlickerDesc: Observe the 20% to 50% dark gray test patches. If brightness pulsates noticeably during refresh transitions, your display exhibits VRR gamma shift.

gtgResponseTimeTest.title: Grey-to-Grey (GtG) Response Time
gtgResponseTimeTest.description: Benchmark pixel transition speeds and identify monitor overdrive inverse coronas.

If monitor overdrive is set too low, trailing ghost blur appears matching the moving block color. If overdrive is set too high (Extreme), excessive voltage pushes liquid crystals past the target state, creating a bright white or dark inverted corona halo. The ideal setting is typically Normal or Fast.
